newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND SAYS FATE OF EMU DECISIVE FOR EU'S FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND SAYS FATE OF EMU DECISIVE FOR EU'S FUTURE.

text.p: The fate of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will determine the future course for the 15-member European Union, Finland -- a staunch EMU supporter -- said in a report on Europe's future.

"Implementation of the third phase of Economic and Monetary Union is a vital cornerstone of the internal market and stable economic development," the government said in the report, which the Finnish parliament started to debate on Wednesday.
EMU would "decisively shape the future of the integration process, and indeed that of the entire European Union," it said.
The third phase of the process towards a single currency should be implemented on schedule from the beginning of 1999, Finland said.
"Any wavering or delay in this process would have a detrimental effect on the stability of the financial markets, and on the future progress of the internal market," it said.
The report acknowledged that the fiscal austerity introduced to improve the resilience of public economies in the run-up to EMU had certain drawbacks.
"This has required and will continue to require adaptation and the attendant costs, one of which is unemployment," it said.
The alternative to implementing economic and monetary union were to postpone it or give up the whole project.

"Either course would be politically difficult, and would have a profound impact on the future of the Union," the report said. "Failure to implement EMU ... would represent a major political disaster," Finland said.
If EMU collapsed, it might "trigger a crisis which the EU in its present form would be unable to solve, drifting into disintegration," it added.
Finland is in favour of including as many nations as possible in the third phase provided that the convergence criteria are interpreted as intended in the Maastricht Treaty.
All EU member states would not be able to meet the criteria in time, while others did not even wish to join, it said.
"The economies of the member states present substantial structural differences, which do not show any sign of narrowing despite all the remedial action taken or planned," Finland said.
EMU would divide the EU countries into at least two different categories.
"The inner circle will enter the third phase of economic and monetary union and adopt a single currency," Finland said.
It did not list which countries belonged to the inner circle, but said the Finnish economy was well on the way to meeting the convergence criteria.
It did not elaborate. Details will be released on Thursday in a finance ministry report on the impact of EMU on the Finnish economy.

The model for different speeds of integration would become institutionalised and give rise to a "completely different kind of Union, in which the member states advance at different speeds and commit themselves to different degrees," the government said.
Certain member states would proceed with more rapidly paced multi-core institutional arrangements, but such arrangements should not be permanent," it added.
The building of monetary union was an investment in the future aimed creating new strength factors in Europe's economies without sacrificing stability, the report said.
Although failure to create EMU could prove fateful, the drive to meet the convergence criteria was important in itself.
"Irrespective of whether the third phase of EMU becomes a reality, greater predictability, economic stability and sound public finances are desirable aims in their own right," it said.
